We're adding a new position in Rubrik, a fast-growing data-security company with an unusually strong combination of growth and cash generation, in the sector that's actually working today. The next big test for the portfolio is whether this week's inflation data cools off or keeps rates rising - that's the macro thread we're watching most closely, since it's the common thread behind today's hardware selloff and the biggest risk to everything we own.

# East Equity Agent — Run 2026-07-13 (14:03 ET, regular full-depth session)

## 1. Macro regime check

Deterministic hint: 4/5, "supportive." I largely agree but with a live caveat. Fed funds is easing
(3.62%, down slightly from 3.64% three months ago, as of 2026-07-09), HY credit spreads are
tightening (2.69% vs 2.94%, as of 2026-07-10), VIX is low and falling (15.03 vs 19.23), and NFCI
shows loose financial conditions (-0.52). The yield curve is not inverted (10y2y +0.38pp, though
flattening from +0.50pp). All of that supports carrying long swing exposure.

The live risk: CPI YoY has re-accelerated sharply to 4.17% (as of 2026-05-01) from 2.43% three
months ago, and both the 10y (4.54%, up from 4.31%) and 2y (4.16%, up from 3.81%) yields are
rising even as the Fed eases — a classic "inflation surprise" combination. Today's tape is a live
example of the risk this creates: headline "Stocks Set to Open Lower as SK Hynix Sparks Chip
Selloff, U.S. Inflation Data and Big Bank Earnings Awaited" (Barchart, 2026-07-13) and "SK Hynix
stock falls, leads broader chip sector declines as AI trade angst returns" are driving a sector-wide,
not company-specific, de-rating in chip/server names today. Regime: supportive for adding, but
I'm discounting high-multiple/long-duration names slightly until the inflation print settles, and I
am treating today's hardware-sector weakness as macro/sentiment-driven rather than fundamental.

## 2. Portfolio review

**Data quality note (important):** the portfolio feed's `last_price` for DELL ($441.90) and HPE
($48.80) is stale relative to two independently-fetched, same-day data points: `position_histories`
shows a 2026-07-13 intraday bar of DELL close $422.17 / HPE close $46.93, and the
`deep_fundamentals` market-cap calc explicitly states "DELL close 423.39 (2026-07-13)" and "HPE
close 46.92 (2026-07-13)," and the options chain spot price agrees (DELL $423.08, HPE $46.92). I am
using ~$423 (DELL) and ~$46.9 (HPE) as today's real prices — both are down roughly 3-6% from my
cost basis and meaningfully closer to their stops than the auto-computed `position_stop_cushion`
field shows (that field was built off the stale quote). Recomputed cushion: DELL is ~0.46 ATR from
its $408 stop, HPE ~0.80 ATR from its $44.75 stop — both now **inside the noise band**. I'm flagging
this as a real cushion, not the friendlier one the tool reported, and deciding deliberately below
rather than treating it as an ordinary day's wiggle.

No forced exits this run.

### DELL — HOLD
Cost basis $450.67, current ~$423.08 (-6.1%), days held 3. Fresh look: Dell's Q1 FY2027 earnings
release (8-K filed 2026-05-28) shows record revenue of $43.8B (+88% YoY), record EPS of $5.24
(+282% YoY), $24.4B in AI orders booked, $16.1B AI-server revenue recognized (+757% YoY), and
management **raised** full-year FY27 revenue guidance to a $165-169B range (midpoint $167B, +50%
YoY) and raised its FY27 AI-server revenue outlook to $60B — both already logged in the guidance
ledger as pending prints to grade at the 9/3 report. The MD&A (10-Q filed 2026-06-09, period end
2026-05-01) confirms the demand story ("substantial demand for our AI-optimized servers... a
significant increase in backlog") but also flags rising input/component costs, which matches the
known quality-ratio deterioration: TTM gross margin 19.16% vs 22.24% prior TTM (period ending
2026-05-01) — a real, already-underwritten risk, not new information.

Today's -6% is not a Dell-specific event: it's the chip/server complex being repriced on
SK Hynix-driven "AI trade angst," and Dell's own top_setups score (7.12) and 3-month sector
momentum (+65.4% avg for servers_hardware) are both still intact even as 1-month momentum has
stalled (+3.3%). Insider activity shows "notable_discretionary_selling" but the overwhelming bulk
of the $636M sell notional (778 trades) is an institutional entity (Silver Lake-linked SPV, likely a
legacy go-private-consortium unwind) — not officers/directors selling on operating concerns; still,
5 discretionary officer/director sells with 0 buys in the window is a fact I'm noting, not dismissing.
13F: no tracked-fund activity either way (neutral, not bearish per the rules). Options market: 11
days to the next expiry, expected move 11.95%, IV 80.5%, skew still calls-bid-over-puts — no
options-market signal of impending further downside.

Cash test: original target $525 implies +24.1% from here; even a reversion to pre-selloff levels
(~$450) is +6.4%. With guidance freshly raised and next earnings 52 days out (outside most of this
hold), the expected return clearly still beats the ~4% cash bar. Thesis intact — holding through a
sector-technical pullback with eyes open on the tightened stop cushion, not moving the stop.

### HPE — HOLD
Cost basis $48.85, current ~$46.92 (-3.9%), days held 2. Q2 FY2026 earnings release (8-K filed
2026-06-01, period end 2026-04-30): record revenue $10.7B (+40% YoY), GAAP gross margin 36.5%
(+810bps YoY), beat its own EPS outlook range, and management **raised full-year FY26 guidance**
and introduced an FY27 growth framework, calling the quarter "two years ahead of our fiscal 2028
long-term financial plan" — this is a genuinely strong print, already logged in the guidance ledger
(FY26Q3 revenue guide $11.5-12.1B pending grade). Same chip-sector rotation dynamic as Dell is
driving today's weakness (HPE down -3.39% in the universe scan's 1-day change, in the same
"servers_hardware" sector that's stalled on a 1-month basis but still +65.4% on 3-month momentum).

Insider signal is "notable_discretionary_selling" but only 1 discretionary officer/director sale in
120 days ($20.4M sell notional total across all filers, mostly small/routine) — this was already
flagged in the original thesis as a single SVP sale, not a cluster, and nothing new has emerged. No
13F tailwind or headwind (no tracked activity). Options: 11 days to expiry, expected move 10.36%,
IV 71.6%, calls-bid-over-puts skew.

Cash test: original target $56.50 is +20.4% from here. Thesis (Juniper synergies, raised guidance,
cheapest multiple in the group at ~12x forward) is fully intact — this was a record quarter, not a
deteriorating one. Holding through the sector wobble, cushion noted as tight.

## 3. Universe scan / candidate selection

Scanned 107 names. Sector relative strength this run: cybersecurity is the strongest complex by a
wide margin (avg 1m momentum +19.1%, 3m +86.5%), well ahead of software_ai (+7.0%/+45.4%) and
servers_hardware, which has clearly stalled on a 1-month view (+3.3%) even with 3-month momentum
still strong (+65.4%) — consistent with today's chip-sector-specific rotation away from hardware
and into software/security.

Top scored setups outside current holdings: NET (7.4), OKTA (7.4), S (7.4), AMD (7.36), RBRK (7.26).
I screened all five (all carry full deep-fundamentals/sec-filings coverage this run):

- **NET (Cloudflare)**: excellent quality (73.79% TTM gross margin, Rule of 40 = 56.6), but
  expensive even by growth-software standards (forward P/E 171x, P/S 41x) and earnings land in 17
  days (2026-07-30) — squarely inside a typical swing hold, creating exactly the binary-print risk
  CLAUDE.md tells me to respect. Watchlist, not a buy today.
- **OKTA**: decent (Rule of 40 47.5), but growth has slowed (fwd revenue growth 9.6%) and the 30-day
  EPS revision is flat/slightly negative. Not a standout versus the alternative below.
- **S (SentinelOne)**: price momentum (+3.61% today, +55.2% 3m) is diverging from its own estimates
  — 30-day EPS revision is -1.72% (down) and Rule of 40 is 38.6 (fails the 40 bar), with a -31.9%
  TTM operating margin. Price up while estimates cut is a red flag, not a green light. Pass.
- **AMD**: spectacular fundamentals (Rule of 40 = 69.5, 44.7% TTM revenue growth) but the stock is
  extended (+120% 3m, +163% 6m) and is today's single worst-hit name in the group (-3.39%), sitting
  at the center of the very chip-sector de-rating described above, with earnings 22 days out
  (inside the hold window — binary risk). Wrong day to chase this one.
- **RBRK (Rubrik)**: the standout. Rule of 40 = 89.1 (66.9% TTM revenue growth + 22.2% TTM FCF
  margin), gross margin expanding sharply (79.82% now vs 69.65% prior TTM, +1017bps), and a net
  cash balance sheet (net debt/EBITDA n/m — net cash, cash $429.4M vs total debt $322.8M as of
  2026-04-30). It's -16.2% off its 52-week high and only -7.6% off its 20-day high — pulling back,
  not extended, with a swing_setup_score of 7.26 (highest of the un-owned names once AMD and NET
  are set aside for the reasons above). It sits in cybersecurity/data-protection, the single
  strongest-momentum sector in this scan today, and (unlike AMD/DELL/HPE) was untouched by the
  chip-specific selloff (-0.98% today, its own idiosyncratic move). Next earnings is 57 days out —
  the first candidate this run where a normal swing hold clears the print entirely.

  Insider activity: "routine_or_sponsor_selling_only" — 69 of 70 sells are 10b5-1 plan trades
  (classic post-IPO lockup-adjacent selling), 0 discretionary officer/director sells, 1 small
  open-market buy. Per the rules this is noise, not a bearish signal, and it's not a buying-cluster
  corroboration either — I'm not overstating it. 13F: no tracked-fund activity (neutral). News flow
  is clean and positive: "Rubrik Launches Agentic-First Rubrik AI Platform" (2026-07-11), a $500M UK
  investment/European HQ announcement (2026-07-09), and "IPO Stock of the Week: Rubrik Flirts With
  Buy Point Amid Path to Profitability" (2026-07-10) — no negative catalysts surfaced. Options:
  expected move 9.82% into the 2026-07-24 expiry, IV 68.1%, balanced put/call skew — no directional
  tilt either way, but nothing bearish. The name is still GAAP-unprofitable (TTM operating margin
  -23.81%) and interest coverage is nominally negative (EBIT still negative, though irrelevant given
  the net-cash position) — the risk here is multiple compression if hyper-growth decelerates, not
  solvency.

RBRK entry ~$83.47 spot. Stop-engineering floor is 5.87% (ATR-based); I'm placing the stop at
~10% below entry (wider than the floor, appropriate for a 45-day swing) rather than at the bare
minimum. Target set near the 52-week high (~$99.6, back-solved from -16.2% off high) at $98.

Weekly self-review: This week was mostly build week, not trade week - the system went from a bare skeleton to a full pipeline (data relay, validator, position sizing, watchlist triggers, insider activity, sector relative strength, post-earnings drift detection) in a handful of commits, and only opened its first two live paper positions on 7/9 (DELL) and 7/10 (HPE). Neither has closed yet, so there is no win/loss to grade - the real test of the process comes next week when these mature past a few days and I have to apply the cash-test and thesis-break discipline for real, not just in theory. What I got right: discipline held under pressure - six separate runs today all correctly said no-trade rather than forcing a mediocre setup into a rate-driven, breadth-thin tape, and both live entries were valuation-anchored (12-20x forward earnings) rather than chases into the 40-170x names topping the momentum scan. What went wrong was mostly data quality, not reasoning: the insider Form-4 feed got flagged as noisy five separate times this week because financial-sponsor distributions (Silver Lake's Dell unwind, ALAB's post-lockup sales) bury genuine officer-conviction signals under hundreds of routine rows, a stale next_earnings field showed a past date for HPE, and the post_earnings_drift_candidate flag missed HPE's textbook drift setup because a one-time GAAP charge masked rising estimates - all bad data, not bad judgment, but they cost research time I'd rather spend on names. The one change for next week: get the insider feed pre-classified into sponsor/10b5-1 vs. discretionary officer transactions before it's handed to me, since that single fix has been the most repeated friction point of the week and is pure engineering, not agent judgment.

** The insider_activity feed is dominated by financial-sponsor unwinds (Silver Lake's programmatic Dell distribution ran to 79 separate line items) and routine 10b5-1 officer sales, which bury any genuinely informative *open-market* signal. A pre-computed classifier flag distinguishing "sponsor/PE distribution" and "scheduled 10b5-1" from "discretionary open-market officer buy/sell," plus a net cluster-buy score, would let me weight this data in seconds instead of scrolling hundreds of near-identical sell tickets to conclude "no signal."

** The insider_activity feed lumps financial-sponsor distributions (Silver Lake's DELL unwind, ALAB's pre-arranged director sales) in with genuine operating-insider signals, forcing me to manually parse dozens of near-identical rows to conclude "not a real signal." A pre-computed classification — tagging each cluster as sponsor/10b5-1-scheduled vs. discretionary officer transaction, and netting to a single per-ticker signal — would make the "clustered officer buying vs. routine selling" judgment the rules ask for far faster and less error-prone.

** The `post_earnings_drift_candidate` flag was `false` for HPE even though it fits the textbook drift profile the bundle prioritizes (record quarter just reported, +40% EPS revisions, price still 24% below its high). The detector appears to have been distorted by HPE's GAAP net *loss* last quarter — a one-time Juniper acquisition charge — which masked the underlying estimate momentum. Adding a "GAAP charge / acquisition-adjusted" screen (or keying the drift flag off EPS-revision magnitude and days-since-earnings rather than reported net income sign) would have surfaced this run's best idea automatically instead of leaving me to reconstruct it by hand.

** The context bundle's per-candidate `next_earnings` field is unreliable — HPE's showed `2026-06-01` (already past) while the `days_to_earnings`/`days_since_earnings` fields correctly implied the next print is in September. These two sources disagreeing forced me to reason around it; the run would be cleaner if `next_earnings` were validated to always be a *future* date (or dropped in favor of the days-based fields), so the earnings-clock gate can't be tripped by a stale value.

** The `insider_activity` feed is dominated by non-signal noise — Silver Lake's sponsor-distribution selling in DELL and Alba/Dyckerhoff post-lockup selling in ALAB swamp the data with hundreds of routine rows, which buries any genuinely informative *officer* buying/selling. This run would have been sharper if the context bundle pre-classified Form 4s (e.g., tagging financial-sponsor/10%-owner distributions and post-IPO-lockup sales separately from discretionary open-market C-suite transactions) and surfaced a net "discretionary officer" buy/sell tally per ticker, so clustered insider *conviction* signals aren't drowned out by mechanical unwinds.

** The context bundle gives me valuation and price/momentum but no consensus estimates or forward revenue-growth figures, so I'm forced to lean on trailing fundamentals plus headline sentiment when judging whether a rich multiple (ANET at 41x, ALAB at 97x) is justified. Adding forward revenue-growth and EPS-revision (analyst estimate trend) fields per candidate would materially sharpen the "is this multiple deserved" call and reduce reliance on qualitative news vibes — the single biggest lever on proposal quality this run.

** The context bundle deep-researches only the top-5 by deterministic score, but two of those five (TXN, AMD) are effectively un-actionable this run because of earnings timing (7/22) or a same-day news gap — meaning I burned my richest data (filings, 13F, news) on names I won't trade, while candidates like HPE and CRDO that I'm actively weighing had only a price and momentum row. Adding a `next_earnings` field and a `days_to_earnings` flag directly into the `universe_scan.top_setups` rows (not just the news block), plus expanding SEC/news enrichment to the top 8 rather than top 5, would let me screen out earnings-binary setups before spending research budget and give me fundamentals on the names I actually end up considering.

** This run would have been materially better with two data additions to the context bundle: (1) a **forward valuation field per candidate** (P/E or EV/S vs. its own 1-yr history) — right now I'm inferring "extended" purely from price momentum, when the real question for the CPI/rate-driven multiple-compression thesis is whether valuations are stretched, and (2) **intraday/1-day price change** so I can distinguish a name resting after a run from one spiking on news *today* (AMD) without cross-referencing headline timestamps by hand. Adding a `pct_change_1d` to the price block and a `valuation` sub-object to each `top_setups` entry would sharpen entry-timing judgment on exactly the chase-vs-wait decisions that dominated this cycle.
